module_2_tissue_hazard_and_heterochrony.module_name: Module 2: Viscoelastic Tissue Hazard & Tendon Heterochrony

baseline_comparison.conclusion: Quasi-static loading yields SF = 2.05 only under isolated zero-rate assumptions at 4800 N. Under dynamic loading (20 kN/s), the 100° flexed posture yields SF = 1.285 < 1.50, failing tissue safety; the 140° extended posture yields SF = 1.747 >= 1.50, but requires extended posture and rigid alignment. Longitudinal tendon reserve SF0 >= 1.776 is an ODE model sensitivity limit, unverified by in vivo human tendon imaging.

inputs.mechanical_workload_kJ: 270 to 810 kJ continuous vs ~70 kJ supra-critical vs ~4 kJ resistance

measured_outputs.transfer_context_limitation: Recovery was measured in Norbury after 3 sets of resistance leg press (4134-5065 kg·reps, not measured in Joules). Force retention at 45 min was 93.01% (LL) and 93.67% (HL), averaging 93.34%. The previously cited '98.3%' and '~4 kJ' were unverified conjectures and have been removed from active conclusions. This cannot be transferred to 2700 s of heavy cycling (619-902 kJ), where sprint training (de Poli SIT, ~70 kJ) causes a 25-29% force drop and fatiguing knee extensions (Kudzia) cause a 25.4% force drop and 4.6x motor control worsening. EXP-0133 decisively proved that neither workload volume nor intensity predicts residual force or power better than simple baselines.

baseline_comparison.conclusion: Volume-based linear fatigue model is strictly refuted by out-of-sample participant-paired bootstrap.

baseline_comparison.conclusion: 4-layer Pennes solver significantly outperforms persistence and lumped capacitance baselines on human heat cycling data.

module_5_motor_control_velocity_power.module_name: Module 5: Motor Control, Velocity Preservation, and Power

measured_outputs.empirical_status_note: CV = 2.1% and COP <= 0.045 m are uncalibrated model proxies. Kudzia et al. (EXP-0111) observed that fatiguing contractions worsened force steadiness CV from 0.61% to 2.83% (failing 2.5% threshold), but raw data were blocked (ISS-0038). Precision grip data were disqualified due to duplicate files (EXP-0124, ISS-0040). Motor control after 2700 s CPE45 remains unassessed in open human datasets.

baseline_comparison.conclusion: Intrinsic shortening velocity adaptation (+12%) overcomes pennation penalty in simulation, preserving velocity within -1.7% and boosting power +19.8%.

TARGET-FORCE20.target: TARGET-FORCE20 (+20% Functional Strength at Comparable Mass)
TARGET-FORCE20.evidence_basis: Strategy 2 musculoskeletal adaptation achieves +21.93% bilateral footplate force at 100° (3130 N vs 2567 N) and +21.77% at 140° (4632.6 N vs 3804.5 N) in gravity-corrected EXP-0090 (+21.64% in legacy EXP-0061). However, in 100° deep flexion under dynamic rate (20 kN/s), local enthesis safety factor drops to SF = 1.285 < 1.50, failing the tissue safety threshold; passing SF = 1.747 is achieved only in extended posture (140°). Steep angular sensitivity gradients (27.59 to 40.98 N/deg) produce a ~410 N artifact at 10° mismatch, and nominal predictions on Santos cohort at 110° exhibit +463.2 N bias, with naive baseline achieving lower MAE by 148 N. In vivo bilateral human transfer remains bounded and unvalidated.
TARGET-FORCE20.operational_boundary: Knee and pelvic posture must be rigidly constrained within ±2° of calibrated task angle; in deep flexion (100°), dynamic rate must be constrained (dF/dt <= 12,000 N/s) or posture extended to >= 140° to prevent enthesis safety factor dropping below 1.50.

TARGET-ADAPT25.evidence_basis: Within-cohort force gain is empirically demonstrated in Santos et al. (SRC-0090), with mean bilateral force increasing +18.35% in 14 days (2525.2 N to 2988.6 N) and +20.01% by Day 42. In tissue ODE simulations, safety factor deficit is eliminated (min SF >= 1.50 across all 42 days) if baseline physiological reserve SF0 >= 1.776, or under Strategy H2 tendon-paced progression. However, because the Santos dataset contains NO comparative control cohort, rate acceleration relative to standard training (+25%) is unproven. Furthermore, human tendon morphology, modulus, and collagen turnover were not measured in vivo.
TARGET-ADAPT25.operational_boundary: Requires native physiological baseline reserve SF0 >= 1.78 or Strategy H2 tendon-paced progression; prospective comparative control cohorts and in vivo ultrasound elastography are required to confirm adaptation rate.

TARGET-CPE45.evidence_basis: TARGET-CPE45 is defined per research/targets/CPE45.json as a 2700 s multi-dimensional requirement. The 4-layer Pennes bioheat solver was empirically validated against in vivo 45-min constant cycling heat data from McLaughlin et al. (SRC-0086, N=23, MAE = 0.586 °C vs persistence 1.275 °C). Simulations of the 360 W x 2700 s scenario (nominal 972 kJ work) confirm that continuous 360 W breaches the 39.5 °C hyperthermia threshold in all climates >= 20 °C (1240–2365 s). Intermittent duty-cycle pacing maintains core temperature < 39.5 °C for 2700 s (D <= 0.59-0.92), but EXP-0065 proved that this thermal feasibility is achieved solely by reducing total mechanical work by 7% to 36% (619-902 kJ vs 972 kJ); at matched work, intermittency showed no thermal advantage. In Norbury et al., post-exercise force retention was 93.01% (LL) and 93.67% (HL) at 45 min after 3 sets of resistance exercise in kg·reps, which cannot be transferred to 2700 s of heavy cycling. Power maintenance, motor control, and post-exercise MVC over 2700 s remain NOT EXTERNALLY VALIDATED.
TARGET-CPE45.operational_boundary: Duty-cycle pacing (D <= 0.59-0.92) across operational climates or active external cooling (>= 420 W); post-load neuromuscular function and motor steadiness require prospective 2700 s human trials.

JOINT_SYSTEM_COMPATIBILITY.target: Overall System Compatibility in Architecture A
JOINT_SYSTEM_COMPATIBILITY.definitive_answer: NO, NOT CONFIRMED AT CURRENT EVIDENCE LEVEL. Simultaneous uncompromised achievement of +20% maximal functional strength, velocity preservation (v_max within -1.7%), peak power elevation (+19.8%), tissue resilience (SF >= 1.50), motor control (CV < 2.5%), and 2700 s CPE45 endurance is NOT empirically demonstrated. In consistent physical simulations, deep flexion (100°) fails dynamic tissue safety (SF = 1.285 < 1.50); continuous 360 W CPE45 fails thermoregulation; intermittent pacing maintains core temperature only by cutting total mechanical work by 7% to 36% and induces neuromuscular fatigue that impairs post-exercise force and motor control; and the +25% acquisition rate lacks a comparative control cohort. Architecture A remains on whole-system HOLD under CONDITIONAL_POTENTIAL.
trade_offs_and_bounds: 1. Posture Bound: Joint angles must be maintained within ±2° during peak force exertion to prevent 28-41 N/deg angular artifacts from degrading the +20% margin; deep flexion (100°) requires dynamic rate limiting (dF/dt <= 12,000 N/s) or posture extension to >= 140° to avoid enthesis shear SF = 1.285 < 1.50.

2. Rate of Force Rise Bound: Explosive ballistic loading must be rate-limited (dF/dt <= 12,000 N/s) or buffered with additional enthesis CSA > 20% to prevent local viscoelastic shear SF dropping below 1.50.

3. CPE45 Thermal Endurance Bound: Sustained 360 W equivalent power must follow intermittent duty cycling (D <= 0.59-0.92) or external cooling (>= 420 W) to avoid core temperature exceeding 39.5 °C, accepting a 7% to 36% reduction in total mechanical work.

4. Bioenergetic Domain Management: High-power work induces neuromuscular and central fatigue; recovery from brief resistance exercise (Norbury 93.01% LL, 93.67% HL at 45 min after 3 sets in kg·reps) cannot be transferred to 2700 s of heavy metabolic endurance without multi-hour recovery windows.

confirmation_rule.formula: (FORCE20 OR ADAPT25) AND (Velocity AND Power AND Tissue Safety AND Motor Control AND CPE45 AND Recovery)

threshold_sources.ADAPT25: Canonical target (+25% rate of strength acquisition vs comparable control; TARGET-ADAPT25)
threshold_sources.Velocity: Working assumption (v_max preservation within -10%; achieved -1.7% in simulation)
threshold_sources.Tissue Safety: Design standard (SF >= 1.50; passes at 140° SF=1.747, fails at 100° dynamic 20 kN/s SF=1.285; unmeasured in vivo)
threshold_sources.Motor Control: Working assumption (CV <= 2.5%, |COP| <= 0.16 m; unassessed over 2700 s)
threshold_sources.CPE45: Canonical target (2700 s alternating explosive/submaximal efforts; TARGET-CPE45, CPE45.json; thermal model validated with work cut; power, motor control, tissue wear, and post-load MVC unmeasured / 'не оценено')
threshold_sources.Recovery: Working assumption (post-load MVC retention >= 90-95%; Norbury achieves 93.34% at 45m; 2700 s metabolic endurance unmeasured)

confirmation_rule.scenario_rejection_boundary: Rejection of an individual scenario (such as continuous 360 W thermal or 100° 20 kN/s dynamic) limits the conclusion strictly to that scenario; justified configurations remain (e.g. intermittent pacing with reduced work, extended 140° posture, rate limiting), but whole-system uncompromised simultaneous satisfaction remains unproven pending decisive in vivo empirical measurements.

decisive_measurements.title: In Vivo Tendon Strain & Modulus Tracking in Rapid Strength Responders
decisive_measurements.modality: High-frame-rate ultrasound elastography + 3T MRI of the patellar tendon during maximal isometric leg press
decisive_measurements.cohort: Rapid strength responders (+15-20% strength gain in 14-28 days)
decisive_measurements.parameters: Regional tendon cross-sectional area, material Young's modulus, enthesis shear strain distribution, collagen cross-linking via UTE-MRI
decisive_measurements.decisive_threshold: Tendon modulus adaptation rate >= 0.005/day and minimum local SF >= 1.50 across all training sessions
decisive_measurements.falsification_condition: Observed in vivo local strain > 6.0% or active collagen microstructural damage under rapid progression

decisive_measurements.title: Synchronous Multi-Angle 3D Kinematics and Multi-Axis Force Dynamometry
decisive_measurements.modality: Synchronous 3D optoelectronic motion capture with dual 6-axis force plates across 80°, 100°, 110°, 120°, and 140° knee angles
decisive_measurements.cohort: Calibrated human cohort (N >= 20) with subject-specific segment geometry and MRI-derived moment arms
decisive_measurements.parameters: Individual joint moments (hip, knee, ankle), footplate center of pressure trajectory x_COP(t), true closed-chain transfer efficiency η_chain
decisive_measurements.decisive_threshold: Elimination of positive model bias (MAE < 200 N across angles) and empirical η_chain >= 0.95 at 100° knee angle
decisive_measurements.falsification_condition: Multijoint transfer efficiency η_chain < 0.85 or inability to maintain COP within safe shoe boundaries (|x_COP| > 0.16 m)

decisive_measurements.title: 2700-s Human Intermittent CPET with Pre- and Post-Exercise MVC in Heat
decisive_measurements.modality: 45-minute intermittent cycling/leg ergometry protocol (D = 0.65–0.92) at 360 W equivalent power in 32°C / 80% RH climate chamber
decisive_measurements.cohort: Trained human endurance athletes (N >= 15) with continuous esophageal/rectal core temperature telemetry
decisive_measurements.parameters: Esophageal temperature T_es(t), VO2, VCO2, sweat rate, and maximal voluntary contraction (MVC) isometric force measured at 0, 5, and 45 minutes post-exercise
decisive_measurements.decisive_threshold: Peak T_core < 39.5°C over 2700 s and post-45-min MVC retention >= 95.0% of baseline pre-exercise MVC
decisive_measurements.falsification_condition: Core temperature exceeding 39.5°C before 2700 s or permanent post-exercise force depression (>10% loss at 45 min)
